headline: Nvidia beat forecasts and raised its outlook after the US close on Tuesday, but bitcoin barely moved from around $64,000 as extreme fear and bets on a December Fed rate rise keep crypto under pressure.

market.asOf: Read at about 23:57 UTC Tue 17 Nov (about 06:57 Wed Bangkok); the pages show no time. BTC from Binance.US ($64,880.91, up 0.02% in 24 hours), ETH from CoinMarketCap ($1,821.13, up 0.13%), SOL from CoinGecko ($74.05, up 3.2%). Prices move fast; use the live prices on this page.

stories.title: Nvidia beats forecasts and guides higher, but crypto barely reacts
stories.summary: Nvidia, the AI chip maker whose results have been moving tech stocks and crypto together, reported sales well above forecasts after the US close and said next quarter should be even bigger. Its shares rose about 2% after hours, but bitcoin hardly moved.
points: Revenue was $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year ago, and data center revenue was $107.6 billion, per Nvidia.
Adjusted earnings were $2.68 a share against about $2.47 expected, per Decrypt; GAAP earnings were $2.70, per Nvidia.
Nvidia expects next quarter's revenue to be $130.0 billion, plus or minus 3%, assuming no data center compute revenue from China; that quarter has an extra week, per Nvidia.
Nvidia shares climbed roughly 2% in after-hours trading, per Decrypt. Bitcoin rose to about $64,500 after the results, per CoinDesk.
Jensen Huang resigned as CEO on 12 Nov and the board is not considering reinstating him; CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO, per Decrypt.

sources.label: Decrypt: Nvidia shares rise on beat

stories.title: Anthropic's share sale nears pricing, due Wednesday
stories.summary: AI company Anthropic is wrapping up orders for its first sale of shares on the stock market and is expected to set the price on Wednesday, with trading on Thursday. Some of the recent crypto selling may have come from investors raising cash to buy in, per an analyst quoted by CoinDesk.
points: Anthropic told investors it expects to price at the top of its $70-78 range or above, per Bloomberg reported by CoinDesk; order books were expected to close at 4pm ET Tuesday.
At $78 a share the company would be valued at about $1.4 trillion and raise more than $90 billion, per CoinDesk.
The sale is 825 million Class A shares, with an option for banks to buy 123.75 million more, per StockTitan.
Pricing is expected on 18 Nov and trading on Nasdaq as ANT on 19 Nov, subject to regulatory clearance, per StockTitan.

stories.title: Bitcoin stuck near $64,000 in extreme fear as fund outflow streak ends
stories.summary: Bitcoin is holding near $64,000, below a long-term average many traders watch, while fear among crypto investors stays extreme. Bitcoin funds stopped a week-long run of withdrawals on Monday, but high interest rates keep buyers cautious.
points: Bitcoin traded around $64,200, below its 200-week average of about $68,000, after a weekend low near $62,000, per CoinDesk.
US spot bitcoin ETFs took in a net $7.9 million on Monday 16 Nov, ending seven straight days of outflows, per Farside data reported by CoinDesk.
XRP fell to about $0.96, its lowest since November 2024, per CoinDesk.
Markets put the odds of a December Fed rate rise at about 92%, and the 10-year Treasury yield is above 5%, per CoinDesk. These are market bets, not a Fed decision.

briefs.title: Binance hack wallets move ether again
briefs.summary: Wallets tied to the Binance hack moved 74,880 ETH (about $136.8M) in about three hours after two quiet weeks, some swapped to BTC via THORChain; Elliptic said only a negligible amount had likely been cashed out, per Decrypt.

briefs.title: Address-swapping code hit 178 brands, including Ledger
briefs.summary: Attackers abused Optimizely to plant code that swapped crypto addresses on sites of 178 brands, stealing about $7,000 by Monday 16 Nov; anyone who visited an affected site that day should check every crypto transfer they made, per Bitcoin.com News.

briefs.title: Tokenized Nvidia trading surges
briefs.summary: Onchain Nvidia perpetual futures have traded more than $22.26B so far in November, about 26 times a year ago, per The Block.

briefs.title: Senate Democrats push back on the CFTC
briefs.summary: Senate Democrats asked the CFTC to withdraw a directive telling prediction markets to stop restricting business by state, saying it conflicts with active court orders, per CoinDesk.
